classification.difficultyReason: Every part is explicitly scaffolded. Part a is routine separation of variables. Part b is the hardest essential step: substitute two data points, divide the equations to eliminate A, and simplify ln(9/4)/2 to ln(3/2). The task tells the student to do this, so little independent planning is needed. Parts c and d are direct substitution and evaluation, with a simplification to (3/2)^t. This is harder than p53-q1, where k comes from a single point once A is known, because here two simultaneous exponential equations must be combined. It is easier than p54-q5, which adds a restructuring and mental-check part, and than p58-q9, where the dividing strategy is not signposted.
